title: Industry-Specific Governance Templates & Benchmarking
explanation: Competitors emphasize deep industry expertise across healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, and government sectors with tailored solutions. Orchestry should develop vertical-specific governance template libraries, compliance presets, and industry benchmarking data that demonstrate maturity compared to peers. This would enable sales teams to lead with industry expertise rather than generic Microsoft 365 capabilities, matching the consultative approach of larger competitors.

title: Advanced AI-Powered Analytics & Employee Engagement Measurement
explanation: While Akumina has 'Advanced Analytics' released, competitors emphasize AI-powered insights, engagement tracking dashboards, and quantifiable ROI metrics (LumApps cites $7.5M productivity gains). Without sophisticated analytics that demonstrate business impact and use AI to surface actionable insights, Akumina may struggle to prove value to C-suite buyers and compete in enterprise deals where ROI justification is critical. The current analytics feature may be insufficient compared to competitor offerings.

title: Frontline Worker-First Positioning & SMS Channel
explanation: Staffbase has differentiated strongly with their 'frontline-first' approach including SMS messaging capabilities, reaching 16.5M employees across non-desk populations. Akumina has the foundational pieces (mobile app, digital signage, multilingual) but lacks SMS capabilities and clear frontline worker messaging. This represents a whitespace opportunity to target the growing frontline worker market (manufacturing, healthcare, retail) with a unified story and missing channel capabilities.

title: AI-Powered Content Creation & Content Pro Tools
explanation: Staffbase offers 'Content Pro' AI-native content management and LumApps provides no-code content creation tools powered by AI, while Akumina relies on traditional CMS workflows. Given that Corporate Communications teams are a primary stakeholder, AI-assisted content creation would dramatically reduce content production time and improve personalization at scale, directly addressing a key user pain point that competitors are already solving.

title: Enterprise AI Agent & Agentic Automation Capabilities
explanation: All three major competitors (Staffbase, LumApps, Viva Connections) are heavily investing in AI-native platforms with AI agents that complete tasks, automate workflows, and provide permission-aware intelligent assistance. Akumina currently only has chatbot integration, which is significantly behind the agentic AI capabilities competitors are offering. Without enterprise AI features, Akumina risks being perceived as outdated in a market where AI is becoming table stakes for employee experience platforms.

title: Accelerate Dynamic Knowledge Pages with AI-Powered Search
explanation: Dynamic Knowledge Pages is currently 'planned' but this should be elevated given that LumApps emphasizes 'permission-aware knowledge retrieval' and agentic search as core differentiators. Knowledge management is foundational to employee experience, and combining the planned Dynamic Knowledge Pages with AI-powered, context-aware search would address a critical competitive gap while leveraging existing roadmap investment.

title: Address trialability and buyer friction before competitors define the category
explanation: ShareGate lowers purchase friction with a full-feature trial and highly established trust signals, while Zenith’s richer governance story may still feel like a bigger adoption commitment. If Zenith does not make time-to-value more obvious through guided onboarding, fast-start assessments, and self-serve proof experiences, competitors may win earlier in the evaluation process even when Zenith is more strategically differentiated.

title: Add bulk remediation actions for governance findings
explanation: ShareGate emphasizes bulk remediation without scripting, which directly targets the same IT admin pain Zenith is replacing. Zenith already detects policy, labeling, lifecycle, and sharing issues well, but expanding from insight to one-click bulk action across sites, libraries, and owners would close an execution gap and strengthen the platform’s control-plane value.

title: Differentiate with MSP-grade cross-tenant benchmarking and fleet operations
explanation: Zenith already has a strong multi-tenant architecture and MSP consent model, which creates a differentiation path ShareGate does not visibly own as strongly in SaaS governance. Productizing tenant fleet benchmarks, policy posture comparison, reusable remediation playbooks, and cross-customer operational dashboards would turn Zenith into the preferred governance operating system for MSPs and multi-brand enterprises.

title: Launch value-proof reporting with quantified ROI and risk reduction metrics
explanation: ShareGate’s messaging is powerful because it translates features into clear operational outcomes such as cutting admin work by 75 percent. Zenith should expose executive-friendly value dashboards that quantify hours saved, risky workspaces remediated, Copilot-ready growth, storage reclaimed, and audit effort reduced so buyers can justify spend and renewal with hard numbers.

title: Expand governance into access drift and oversharing remediation
explanation: Zenith has strong sharing link discovery and Copilot readiness, but ShareGate’s positioning around oversharing detection and access drift visibility is highly resonant in the current AI-readiness market. Adding continuous monitoring of permission drift, excessive membership exposure, and risky access changes—with guided remediation—would make Zenith more competitive in security-led Microsoft 365 buying cycles.
